# Yield Forecast Modeling

Yield forecast modeling predicts crop quantities in vertical farms using statistical and machine learning methods. It analyzes input variables like nutrient dosing levels, light intensity, temperature, and historical yields to estimate upcoming harvest weights. Models range from linear regressions to complex neural networks, balancing interpretability and accuracy.

For example, a regression model might use past data showing that increasing nitrogen dosing by 5% increases yield by 0.3 kg per grow tower. If the baseline yield is 10 kg, the forecasted yield becomes 10.3 kg.

Tradeoffs include data quality dependence, model complexity, and adaptability to changing conditions. Common failures arise from sensor errors, unmodeled pests, or sudden environmental shifts causing inaccurate predictions. Regular retraining and sensor calibration are essential for reliability.
